 ORDER
With the consent of parties, the matter is heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal by the owner under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 24.01.2015 passed by Ist MACT, Chhatarpur in MACC No.02/2013 seeking reduction of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal and exonerated from liability to pay the compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned Tribunal has wrongly held that present accident was caused by offending vehicle.
Learned Tribunal has wrongly held that appellant is liable to pay the compensation and has wrongly exonerated Insurance Company from liability to pay the compensation.
On above grounds, it is urged that appeal filed by appellant be allowed.
4. Learned counsel for the respondents No.1,2 and 3 has submitted that Tribunal has wrongly exonerated Insurance Company from liability to pay the compensation.

5 . Learned counsel for the respondent No.4-Insurance Company has submitted that award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper and it has rightly exonerated respondent Insurance Company from liability to pay the compensation.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. Perusal of order-sheet dated 04.07.2022 reveals that application filed by appellant under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC has been allowed and document filed along with the I.A. has been taken on record.
8.
In view of above order, it would be just and proper to remand the case to afford opportunity of adducing evidence to both the parties with respect to documents taken on record vide above order.

9. Hence, appeal filed by the appellant is allowed and impugned award is set aside and Tribunal is directed to afford opportunity to appellant to adduce evidence with respect to documents filed by him along with I.A.No.6799 of 2022 (Order 41Rule 27 CPC) and thereafter, afford opportunity to Om Prakash Prajapati vs Vidya Devi Ahirwar on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128846970/
2 claimants as well as respondent-Insurance Company etc. to adduce evidence in rebuttal, if any, and thereafter, after affording opportunity to both the parties of hearing, decide the case afresh on merits.
10.
